hints: Use one partial-fraction term for the linear factor and one for each power of the repeated factor.
Use $x=-\tfrac12$ and $x=3$ to isolate two constants directly.
Find the remaining constant using another convenient value such as $x=0$, then substitute all three constants into the decomposition.
walkthrough:
State the form of the partial fractions for $f(x) = \dfrac{21 - 8x - 2x^2}{(1 + 2x)(3 - x)^2}$:
$$\dfrac{21 - 8x - 2x^2}{(1 + 2x)(3 - x)^2} = \dfrac{A}{1 + 2x} + \dfrac{B}{3 - x} + \dfrac{C}{(3 - x)^2}$$

Multiply through by the common denominator $(1 + 2x)(3 - x)^2$:
$$21 - 8x - 2x^2 = A(3 - x)^2 + B(1 + 2x)(3 - x) + C(1 + 2x)$$

Substitute $x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ to isolate and find $A$:
$$21 - 8\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = A\left(3 - \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)^2$$
$$21 + 4 - \dfrac{1}{2} = A\left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2$$
$$\dfrac{49}{2} = \dfrac{49}{4}A \implies A = 2$$

Equate the coefficients of $x^2$ to find $B$:
$$-2 = A - 2B$$
$$-2 = 2 - 2B$$
$$2B = 4 \implies B = 2$$

State the complete partial fractions expansion:
$$f(x) = \dfrac{2}{1 + 2x} + \dfrac{2}{3 - x} - \dfrac{3}{(3 - x)^2}$$

hints: Expand each partial fraction from part (a) separately as a binomial series through $x^2$.
Rewrite the other denominators with $3-x=3(1-x/3)$, then use the expansions of $(1-x/3)^{-1}$ and $(1-x/3)^{-2}$.
Multiply by the coefficients from part (a), collect the constant, $x$, and $x^2$ contributions, and discard higher powers.
walkthrough:
Expand the first partial fraction $2(1 + 2x)^{-1}$ up to $x^2$ using the binomial series $(1 + u)^{-1} = 1 - u + u^2 - \dots$:
$$2(1 + 2x)^{-1} = 2(1 - 2x + (2x)^2) = 2(1 - 2x + 4x^2) = 2 - 4x + 8x^2$$

Expand the second partial fraction $\dfrac{2}{3 - x} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-1}$ up to $x^2$:
$$\dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-1} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{3} + \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{x^2}{9}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{9}x + \dfrac{2}{27}x^2$$

Expand the third partial fraction $-\dfrac{3}{(3 - x)^2} = -\dfrac{3}{9}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-2} = -\dfrac{1}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-2}$ up to $x^2$:
$$\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-2} = 1 + (-2)\left(-\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + \dfrac{(-2)(-3)}{2}\left(-\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2 = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x + \dfrac{1}{3}x^2$$
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x + \dfrac{1}{3}x^2\right) = -\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{2}{9}x - \dfrac{1}{9}x^2$$

Sum the corresponding terms across all three expansions:
$$\text{Constant term: } 2 + \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3} = 2 + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{7}{3}$$
$$\text{Term in } x: -4x + \dfrac{2}{9}x - \dfrac{2}{9}x = -4x$$
$$\text{Term in } x^2: 8x^2 + \dfrac{2}{27}x^2 - \dfrac{3}{27}x^2 = \left(8 - \dfrac{1}{27}\right)x^2 = \dfrac{215}{27}x^2$$
